ai.description: *Ichthyophis alfredi* reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pale venter. Key features include a blunt snout and 280–300 primary annular grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis alfredi* is best distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail, unlike many other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis alfredi* inhabits moist, evergreen tropical forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in damp soil near streams at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: Alfred’s Striped Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil after rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis alfredi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs in terrestrial burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with maternal attendance.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis alfredi* is endemic to the Garo Hills in the Indian state of Meghalaya, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis alfredi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched clicks, typically emitted while the animal is submerged in shallow forest streams.
